# Orchestrations / O4I - flows, node vocabulary, limits, call patterns

INTEGRATION apps (`wdcli app create --app-type INTEGRATION`) contain only `appManifest.json` + `orchestration/*.orchestration`. Extend apps can also carry orchestrations alongside their presentation layer.

## The .orchestration format ("Maya" engine) - and how to author it

Single JSON doc: `{"flowVersion": "3.1.0", "_type": "Flow", "_value": {...}}` where EVERY value is a typed-AST envelope `{"_type": <TypeName>, "_value": <payload>}`. Verbose and ID/position-sensitive - a serialized syntax tree, not hand-friendly config. The root can also carry `securityDomains: ["<Domain>"]` - this is what an `enabledForOrchestrationSecurity` domain in the `.securitydomain` file pairs with to gate who can launch the flow (verified in a delivered production app, 2026-08-05).

**The orchestration launch gate is a BARE array at the FLOW ROOT - a sibling of `"_type": "Flow"`, OUTSIDE the `_value` AST.** Working shape: `"securityDomains": ["<Domain>"]` on the outermost object. **CONFIRMED end-to-end (a delivered app, 2026-08-07): adding the bare root array built AND deployed cleanly.** Corroborated 2026-08-07 by reading Workday sample apps in a dev tenant: `.pmd`, `.businessobject`, and `.businessprocess` all serialize `securityDomains` as a bare string array (`["ManageCreateAnEvent"]`), and orchestrations that don't gate simply omit the root key.

**Two look-alikes named `securityDomains` - do not confuse them:**
- **The gate (what you edit):** a bare `"securityDomains": ["<Domain>"]` at the OUTER root, sibling of `"_type": "Flow"`. This is what pairs with an `enabledForOrchestrationSecurity` domain to gate who can launch the flow.
- **A benign tooling artifact:** the Builder also emits a NESTED `securityDomains: {"_type": [Opt,[List,String]], "_value": null}` *inside* the flow's `_value`. Leave it null and untouched - apps build and run fine with it; it is NOT the gate. A working file carries BOTH at once.
- **Exception - check the file before assuming (seen 2026-10-07, a flowVersion 2.16.0 app as downloaded from the platform):** every flow carried NO root key and a POPULATED nested list instead, `{"_type":["Opt",["List","String"]],"_value":{"_type":["List","String"],"_value":[{"_type":"String","_value":"<Domain>"}]}}`. It is the only domain declaration in those files, so it is taken to be the gate. That is inferred from the source: a launch refused because of it has not been reproduced. In such a file, change the domain inside the nested list rather than adding a root key, and keep the file's existing form. Read `d["_value"]["securityDomains"]` first; a populated nested list is the gate there.
- **ONE security domain per flow - a hard build error (build-verified 2026-10-07, Orchestrate Compiler 3.400.0).** A second entry in the nested list failed the build with "At /securityDomains: Only one security domain can be defined for an orchestration". To let a second population launch a flow, change the launch instead: swap the single domain, change the page endpoint's `authType` (`sso` checks the user, `isuAuth` checks the ISU), or change the grants. Note that a launch-auth change is a security decision: it changes who the platform checks at launch. `scripts/pmd_preflight.py` now fails any flow that names two or more domains (`flow-domains`).

**This fully explains a real build failure (built 3x-fail then reverted):** that edit set the NESTED envelope's `_value` to a bare list (`["AppLead"]`) - wrong field AND wrong shape. Fix = add the bare array at the outer root and leave the nested typed-null alone. (The failure also wore the transient-instant signature - see the retry-vs-bisect note in [wdcli-workflow.md](wdcli-workflow.md); note a SINGLE same-second failure can still be genuine flake, so retry once, and only bisect after ~3 identical failures.)

**Authoring approach that works (build-verified):** generate the JSON from a Python builder script with small helper functions per node type, rather than hand-editing. Copy a proven template app (`wdcli app copy`), keep its reusable subflows verbatim (e.g. a SendSOAPRequest subflow + EventSummary subflow), delete unused subflow files, and emit a new main flow that calls them. Reference implementation: a `generate_flow.py` builder script kept alongside the app in your Extend workspace.

**Hand-authored `.maya.FlowSync` JSON (donor-clone path) also builds clean** - a bulk PATCH loop + two-pass POST-then-PATCH compiled on Orchestrate Compiler 3.367 when the source JSON was cloned from a working FlowSync and edited by hand (fields changed, nodes adjusted). Confirm the Compiler version in your target tenant matches before relying on this; schema tolerance can vary between versions. (Verified in a delivered build session, 2026-08-18.)

**Claude's realistic role:** full wdcli lifecycle [x]; editing logic in existing flows (expressions, XPaths, API versions, conditions, adding a log/branch node) [x]; hand-authoring a brand-new flow from scratch (!) - prefer the visual Orchestration Builder for net-new flow layout, then code for edits, review, and promotion. Run the structural linter (`scripts\validate.py` in the workspace; regenerate it from [scripts.md](scripts.md) if absent) before every upload of generated JSON.

## How pages invoke flows - the `/launch` bridge (verified in delivered production apps, 2026-08-05)

Every PMD<->flow call hits `.../orchestrate/v1/apps/<appId>/orchestrations/<flowName>/launch`. Wire it once as an AMD dataProvider, then use relative URLs per endpoint:

```json
{ "key": "workday-orchestration",
  "value": "<% `{{apiGatewayEndpoint}}/orchestrate/v1/apps/{{site.applicationId}}/orchestrations/` %>" }
```

- **Read (sync GET):** inbound endpoint `"url": "Get_Instances_X/launch?Reference_ID_Type=Attendance_Status_ID"` - the flow reads query params via `data.start.queryParams.getParam("Reference_ID_Type", emptyString())`.
- **Write (POST):** an `outboundEndPoints[]` entry with `httpMethod: "POST"`, `url: "/Orch_PostDataToBO/launch"`, `onSend` returning the JSON body. The flow reads it via `data.start.request.asJSON().stringAtJsonPath(...)` / `arrayAtJsonPath(...)`, or declares a typed `structuredRequest` (ObjectRequestStructure) on `StartBasic`.
- **Named launch params on StartBasic (build + runtime verified, 2026-08-05):** declare them in `start.structuredRequest.ObjectRequestStructure.props` as a `Map<String, RequestStructure>` - each a `PrimitiveRequestStructure` (type String, optional default like `emptyString()`); nested objects use a nested `ObjectRequestStructure`. The launch POST body carries values by name (`{"startDate": "2026-10-05"}`), and expressions read them as **`data.start.$_<paramName>`** - e.g. `s"""${"SELECT ... WHERE mainTask in ("}${data.start.$_WID}${")"}"""`; `date.parse(data.start.$_startDate, """yyyy-MM-dd""")` accepts the param string directly. This is the clean way to pass ids/dates from a page into an in-app flow.
- **Two DIFFERENT input mechanisms, keyed to the start type:** `data.start.$_x` on `StartBasic` = launch-BODY params (page/REST launch, no ISU needed) / `lp.booleanParam(...)/dateTimeParam(...)/integrationSystemId()` on `StartIntegrationFrameworkTrigger` = INTEGRATION-SYSTEM launch parameters (need the ISU/ISSG + tenant integration-system config). Don't mix the syntaxes across start types.
- Bulk-body assembly idioms: `"{\"data\": ".append(data.Loop.item.toString()).append("}").asJSON()` builds a bulk wrapper from a folded array; `.remove("$.total")` strips a collection wrapper's metadata before re-posting.
- **Async flows launch the same way** (`/orch_Async_submitX/launch`) - the page gets an immediate ack; the work escapes the 25 s page-sync cap.
- **Home Cards launch flows through the same `StartBasic`/`/launch` bridge as a page** - a `.carddefinition` footer `taskReference` drives the task, and a card-triggered `.maya.FlowSync` runs under the **20-min Home-Card budget** (see Runtime limits), NOT the 25 s page-sync cap - so a card is the place for a heavier user-triggered sync flow. (Per Workday App Catalog sample employeeRecognition home cards.)
- **Response (`EndSync` body):** either `DataRefBody` pass-through - including `response.asXML().fragmentAtXPath(...)`, i.e. a SOAP fragment handed straight back to the page and consumed as JSON - or `CreateJsonBody` with a `JsonTemplateRef` + mappings.
- `apiGatewayEndpoint` is a built-in AMD variable; note the backtick-`{{}}` templating inside dataProvider values.

## Node vocabulary (build-verified)

- Flow types -> start/end nodes (source-verified across delivered production apps, 2026-08-05): `.maya.FlowSync` -> `StartBasic`/`EndSync` / `.maya.FlowAsync` -> `StartAsync`/**`EndEmptyMaya`** (async flows do NOT use `EndSync` - they ack immediately and run headless, so there's no sync response body; per Workday App Catalog sample employeeRelationsIncidentManagement, flowVersion 3.2.0) / `.maya.FlowBusinessProcessTriggered` -> `StartBusinessProcess` (typed parameters with default expressions, e.g. `Effective_Date = date.now().toString()`; actual values bind on the tenant BP-step config) / `.maya.IntegrationFrameworkTrigger` -> `StartIntegrationFrameworkTrigger`/`EndEmptyMaya` (carries `configureForRetrieval: false` unless it's a retrieval-configured inbound) / `.maya.FlowSubflow` -> `StartSubflow` (typed parameters)/`EndSubflow` (exports), stored in **`.suborchestration`** files. There is no `MixedStart` at flowVersion 3.x; a legacy `.Mixed.MixedFlow` start exists in 2.x flows only (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified) - never emit a new one. Convention: an `IN_PROGRESS_`-prefixed flow name marks a stub that must not be scheduled.
- `CreateValues` - assign typed variables (the workhorse) / `CreateJson` - build a JSON document (source-verified in a delivered async flow, 2026-08-05)
- `CreateTextTemplate` - build text/XML/JSON payloads; `{{ data.X.y }}` interpolation; supports logic blocks `{{#each}}`/`{{#if}}`/`{{!--comment--}}` with `\\` at block-tag line ends to suppress newlines - this is how multi-line SOAP bodies are built from JSON arrays
- `SendWorkdayApiRequest` - Workday SOAP/REST (path like `/soap/v46.1/Financial_Management`; auth via WorkdayCredentialRef - see auth below)
- `SendHttpRequest` - EXTERNAL HTTP (full `url`, `auth: [Opt, ExternalAuthRef]` - null + explicit Authorization header is common; `tlsConfigRef` is flowVersion-dependent: 3.1.0 flows omit it, 3.3.0 flows carry `tlsConfigRef: _DEFAULT_TLS_CONFIG` - verified in delivered production apps; omit `pollingConfigRef` at 3.1.0)
  - **[BV] A `SendHttpRequest` node FAILS THE BUILD at flowVersion 3.2.0** ("Build failed with errors", no validation detail); the SAME flow bumped to 3.3.0 (only change) builds first try. The external-HTTP node schema rides on `flowVersion`, NOT on app-type or flow-type: an Extend app CAN egress from its own orchestrations, and a `.maya.FlowSync` sync flow CAN egress - both fine at 3.3.0. Rule: author ANY flow containing `SendHttpRequest` at `flowVersion` 3.3.0, or clone the whole top-level scaffold from a known-good 3.3.0 donor. Workday-only flows (SendWorkdayApiRequest only) build fine at 3.2.0. Note the build system is flaky (identical source can fail then build) - a genuine schema error like the 3.2.0 `SendHttpRequest` fails deterministically (3/3), transient flake does not.
  - **[BV] `intsys.*` integration-system attribute reads are NOT available inside a SYNC (`.maya.FlowSync`) flow** - a sync flow reading `intsys.stringAttributeValue(...)` fails the build. `intsys` (the integration-system attribute store) is valid only in integration/event-triggered flows. In a sync/page-invoked flow, pass config in the launch request (`data.start.request.asJSON()`) or read the app's App Attributes (`attrstore.stringValue(...)`) / an applicationAttributes BO via `SendWorkdayApiRequest`.
- `SendIntegrationMessage` - write to the integration event log (severity, `condition`-gated - the Debug-logging pattern)
- `BranchOnConditions` (ifBranches of WhenBranch + elseBranch) / `Loop` / `BatchLoop` (batchStrategy + foldValue; batch exposed as `data.<Loop>.batch`) / fold types (our build-verified core): Count/Sum/String/Json
  - **Aggregate/foldValue fold taxonomy (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified) - the fuller set:** `JsonFoldValue`, `CountFoldValue`, `TextFoldValue`, `StringFoldValue`, `XmlFoldValue`, `SumFoldValue`, `NumberFoldValue`, `StringMapFoldValue`, `CsvFoldValue`, `FormattedCsvFoldValue`, `ZipArchiveFoldValue`, `BooleanFoldValue`. (Csv/FormattedCsv/Xml/ZipArchive are the ones our core list omitted - reach for FormattedCsv/Zip when building file payloads in a Loop. `BooleanFoldValue` ORs a boolean across a loop = "did ANY iteration fail?" - canonical `orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/Install.orchestration`, `nameProp "HadError"`, 2026-08-07.)
  - **`data.<Loop>.itemNumber` runtime iteration counter - sample-verified (canonical DevRel samples, 2026-08-07; build-verify in-tenant before production reliance).** A per-iteration counter on `Loop`/`BatchLoop`/`JoinLoop`, numeric, commonly `.format("0")` or `.toString().leftPad(4,"0")` for padded sequence IDs (`orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/ImportProcessor.orchestration`; `workerInboundImageUpload/.../WorkerPhotoInbound.orchestration` uses `data.PhotoLoop.itemNumber` + `data.JoinLoop.itemNumber`; `CreateExcel.suborchestration` uses `math.plus(3, data.repack.itemNumber)`). Does NOT conflict with the Loop CONFIG-key census below - `itemNumber` is a runtime OUTPUT, not a config key, so both hold. This is the clean way to generate sequential row numbers / padded IDs inside a loop.
- `ContinueOnConditions` - assertion gate; failing inside a group with an ErrorHandler skips just that iteration
- `ErrorHandler` - group-level (`data._group_X.isSuccess` / `.processingError.rawMessage()`) or GlobalErrorHandler (flow-level, `data._orchestration.processingError`); strategy enum + `.locationId`/`.locationPath` per the caveat above
- `CallSubflow` (subflowId + parameters; inside the subflow read `data.start.<Param>`) / `StoreDocument` (tags, `storageExpiresIn` like `P7D`, delivery) / `Group` (`Assertion` is NOT a standalone node - it is a sub-object of `ContinueOnConditions`; see orchestration-nodes.md)
- `Validate` node anatomy (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified): a list of `ValidationCheck` rules, each a boolean `condition` expression + a `message` + a `ValidationSeverity` - a rule that fails ERROR halts the flow (like `ContinueOnConditions` but with declared messages); use it as the named-rule input gate at the top of a write flow. Outputs (confirmed 2026-08-07, `orchestrationToolkit/orchestration/ValidateWithValidationIterator.orchestration`, `supplierInvoicesInbound/.../INT_Supplier_Invoices_Orch_Inbound.orchestration`): `data.<Validate>.allValid` (boolean) and `data.<Validate>.failedValidations` (iterable - Loop it to surface each failed message to the caller).
- `JoinLoop` - source-verified (2026-08-05): joins one dataset against another inside a batch pipeline (e.g. per-worker RaaS rows against config rows)
- `TriggerIntegration` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified) - launch a CHILD integration (Studio / EIB / Core Connector) from a flow; target it via `instanceRef.integrationReference()`. The orchestration-native way to chain an O4I onto a legacy packaged integration. **Full invoker (confirmed 2026-08-07, `orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/TriggerIntegration.orchestration` + `ImportProcessor.orchestration`):** pass TYPED launch params to the child via `IntegrationLaunchParameterMapping` with `TextLaunchParameterValue` / `DateTimeLaunchParameterValue` / `InstanceReferenceLaunchParameterValue`, and read the child's OUTPUT documents back into the parent with `data.<Node>.childDocuments.iterator()` / `.childDocuments.name("import_id.xml").get().asXML().stringAtXPathOrEmptyString("//wd:ID")`. So a parent flow can launch a child integration, feed it parameters, and harvest its result file - not just fire-and-forget.
- `SendPrismRequest` - **RE-CONFIRMED sample-verified (2026-08-25).** The typed node EXISTS: 6 instances in the local App Catalog (`salesCommission/orchestration/executeDCT.suborchestration` + `executeDCTFromFile.suborchestration`), used for DCT (Data Change Task) execution - shape in orchestration-nodes.md. The 2026-08-07 "appears NOWHERE" downgrade was itself wrong (the token search that produced it missed these files). BOTH facts hold: the canonical file-LOAD flow (`prismAndExtendDesignPatterns/loadPrismByFileSync.orchestration`) uses raw `SendWorkdayApiRequest` against `prismAnalytics/v3/fileContainers` -> `/files` -> `dataChanges/.../activities`, while DCT EXECUTION uses the typed `SendPrismRequest`. Pick by verb: raw REST for container/file loads, the typed node for running a DCT. (History kept as a propagation-rule case study: a "disproven" note can itself be the error - cite files, not absence.)
- `ConvertXmlToJson` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified) - a typed node that converts an XML/SOAP response to JSON; pair with **`.unwrapSoap()`** to strip the SOAP envelope before the conversion so downstream `stringAtJsonPath` reads land on the operation body, not the envelope.
- `SendWorkdayRestApiPaginationRequest` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified - this is the real name of the "paged REST call" component below) - auto-pages a Workday REST collection: set `limit`/`offset`/`maxPages` and it `flatten`s the pages into one dataset, so you skip the manual CreateValues+Send+Loop paging loop. Upgrades the (!) paged-call note in "Reading data at scale" from shape-unverified to sample-verified.
- `SendWwsPaginationApiRequest` (confirmed 2026-08-07, `supplierInvoicesInbound/.../INT_Check_Import_Result_Orch.orchestration`) - the SOAP counterpart to the REST pagination node: auto-pages a WWS operation's multi-page response (e.g. `Get_Import_Process_Messages`). Use it for SOAP reads that page (the REST node above is for `/api` REST collections).
- `TriggerPdfGeneration` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified - was course-documented/shape-unverified): generates a PDF from a template + data binding inside a flow; combine with a `ZipArchiveFoldValue` fold to bundle many generated PDFs into one archive for delivery.
- **Attachment-IN (multipart) - `FormDataBody` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified):** to POST a file INTO Workday (or an external multipart endpoint) from a flow, build a `FormDataBody` (the multipart/form-data body type) with the file part + field parts, rather than a JSON/text body. This is the inbound counterpart to the base64 attachment-out pattern below.
- Course-documented, JSON shape unverified: Integration Maps (`intsys.mapLookup("<Map>", key)` - set a Default Value or unmatched keys throw)

**Caveat - `SendWorkdayApiRequest` does NOT hard-fail on 4xx (HIGH, silent data loss).** A create POST the BO rejects produces no flow error - the flow "completes clean" with 0 records written. A clean completion is NOT proof anything was written. Always check the response status explicitly (or gate the write with `ContinueOnConditions` / an `ErrorHandler`) before trusting a create succeeded; don't infer success from the flow finishing. Concrete guards (verified in delivered production apps, 2026-08-05): REST - `data.<Send>.responseStatusCode == 200`; SOAP - `data.<Send>.response.asXML().isValueAtXPath(".../SOAP-ENV:Fault/faultstring")`; and give every risky node a per-node `errorHandler` with a strategy, e.g. `{"strategy": "PropagateError", "nodes": [Log ... data.<Node>.processingError.toString()]}`.

- **The declarative fix - `retryConfig.successResponseCodeRanges` (build-verified, billonly-v2 Submit_Requisition_Orch; shape in orchestration-nodes.md).** A retry-config resource can declare which HTTP status ranges count as SUCCESS; a response OUTSIDE those ranges is then treated as a real failure the node raises on (so a 4xx finally hard-fails instead of completing clean). Anatomy: `successResponseCodeRanges` is a TOP-LEVEL key of the `retryConfig` (a sibling of `maxTotalRetries`, `defaultBackOff`, and `retryPolicies[]`), holding ResponseCodeRange objects `[{"begin":200,"end":299}]` (keys are `begin`/`end` - an earlier example here said `low`/`high` AND nested this under `retryPolicies[]`; both corrected 2026-08-25 against all 18 corpus ResponseCodeRange instances). The separate `retryPolicies[]` list holds the per-status-code retry/backoff policies. Reference the config on the Send node. This is the config-level complement to the per-node `responseStatusCode`/XPath-fault guards above - declare the success ranges so undeclared codes stop silently succeeding. The samples ship three named defaults referenced by Send nodes: **`_DEFAULT_WORKDAY_RETRY_CONFIG`** (in-tenant Workday API calls), **`_DEFAULT_EXTERNAL_RETRY_CONFIG`** (external HTTP), and **`_DEFAULT_INTEGRATION_RETRY_CONFIG`** (integration-system calls) - reuse the matching default rather than hand-rolling ranges. (`_DEFAULT_WORKDAY_RETRY_CONFIG` already appears on our SOAP `Get_Worker_Photos` fetch; the `successResponseCodeRanges` semantics are the catalog-sourced detail.)
- **`ErrorHandler` strategy enum (per Workday App Catalog samples):** `PropagateError` (raise to the flow), `GlobalErrorHandler` (route to the flow-level handler), `ConditionalOutputs` (branch on the error without failing). A raised error exposes **`.locationId`** and **`.locationPath`** (which node/step failed) alongside `.processingError.rawMessage()` - use them to log WHERE the failure occurred. **Journal-then-compensate rollback idiom:** on a multi-write flow, journal each successful write (id + verb) as you go, and in the error handler replay the journal in reverse to compensate (delete/PATCH-back the already-committed rows) - O4I has no transaction, so this is how you unwind a partial bulk write.

## Expression language (inside `source` strings - the real "code")

- Node outputs: `data.<NodeName>.<param>`; launch params `lp.booleanParam("X")`, `lp.referenceData("Worker","WID")`; integration attributes `intsys.stringAttributeValue("Attr")`
- **Function-form node access `data("<Node>","<param>")` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified)** - the same read as `data.<Node>.<param>` but with the node/param names as STRING args; use it when a name isn't a valid dotted identifier or must be built dynamically. Also `system.apiGatewayEndpoint()` - the flow-side accessor for the gateway base URL (the expression-language sibling of the AMD `apiGatewayEndpoint` dataProvider variable), for composing `.../orchestrate/...` or portable BO paths inside a flow.
- **Launch-as-GET read (per Workday App Catalog samples, confirms our existing pattern):** a page can call `.../<flow>/launch?X=y` as a GET and the flow reads `data.start.queryParams.getParam("X", emptyString())` - same bridge documented under "How pages invoke flows".
- **Nested launch params flatten to `$_<prop>_<nested>` (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified).** A nested `ObjectRequestStructure` on `StartBasic` exposes its leaves with the path underscored: a `filters.dateFrom` param reads as `data.start.$_filters_dateFrom` (each nesting level adds an `_<prop>` segment). Extends our flat `data.start.$_<paramName>` note for structured launch bodies.
- **App Attributes: `attrstore.stringValue("subscriptionKey")`** - the app-level attribute store (source: `attributes/default.attributes`), readable from flows AND pages; distinct from `intsys.*` integration-system attributes. Good home for secrets, endpoints, even the SOAP API version (verified in delivered production apps, 2026-08-05).
- **Tenant-portable BO REST paths: `context.appReferenceId()`** - `s"${"/apps/"}${context.appReferenceId()}${"/v1/<collection>"}"`; `.capitalize()` builds the app's reference-ID prefix (see reference-ID addressing below).
- Scala-like interpolation `s"${a}${b}"`; helpers: `.isBlank()`, `.toInt()`, `.split(",")`, `date.parse(s,"MM/dd/yyyy")`, `.substringAfterLast(".")`, `.base64MimeDecode(ct)`, `if (cond) a else b`; math `math.div/mult/minus`, `.toNumber().toDouble()`, `.lessThanOrEquals()`; boolean chaining `.and()/.not()`; `.append()`
- **Date arithmetic WORKS here (unlike PMD): `date.parse("2026-01-01","yyyy-MM-dd").plusDays(10)` -> `2026-01-11`** (build + runtime verified in-tenant, 2026-08-05). The parsed value behaves as a JVM LocalDate-like object and coerces to ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` when interpolated into a string. THE way to resolve relative dates ("start + N days", "due in 7 days") that PMD's five `date:` functions can't - pages hand the inputs to a flow; the flow computes. Inside `s""` interpolation use triple-quoted literals for the args: `s"${date.parse("""2026-01-01""","""yyyy-MM-dd""").plusDays(10)}"`.
- XML: `data.X.response.asXML().stringAtXPath("/env:Envelope/.../wd:File")`; JSON: `stringAtJsonPath(WithDefault)`, `numberAtJsonPath`, `booleanAtJsonPath`, `arrayAtJsonPath(WithDefault)`, `countItemsAtJsonPath`, `numbersAtJsonPath(...).sum()`, `stringsAtJsonPath(...).mkString(".")`, `jsonDataAtJsonPath`, `isValueAtJsonPath`, `.iterator("$.data[*]")`, `"[]".asJSON()` (empty-array literal), `isDataDefined("Node","param")`. **DANGER: use `*WithDefault` variants whenever the path may be absent.** The non-default (throwing) variants (`stringAtJsonPath`, `numberAtJsonPath`, etc.) throw an exception when the path is absent -- the flow dies on that step EVERY TIME with no visible error message, and any orchestration that writes status back never runs. Observed: a flow reading `header.position` with `stringAtJsonPath` where checkout had never stamped position caused zero statuses ever written across dozens of test runs (build+deploy verified, UAP v2, 2026-08-31). Always prefer `stringAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.field", emptyString())` for optional fields.
  - **`isDataDefined("start", "param")` is a BUILD ERROR** ("There is no upstream component with id start") - `start` is not a node. Read declared subflow/launch params by dotted path `data.start.<param>` and guard an optional one with a top-level `if`: `if (s"${data.start.runId}".isBlank()) <fallback> else s"${data.start.runId}"` (build-verified). (The `isDataDefined("Node","param")` form above is only for actual upstream node outputs.)
- **How `SendHttpRequest` + `asJSON()` behave on a broken vendor (log-verified 2026-10-07, a client app).** (1) **Unresolvable host:** the send step FAILS ("Unable to resolve IP address from URL", after the retry config is exhausted), and `data.<Send>.responseStatusCode` then does not exist - any later step that reads it fails with "Referenced output 'responseStatusCode' ... does not exist in data context". (2) **403 with an HTML body:** the send step does NOT fail, and `response.asJSON()` does not check the body - it wraps it ("JsonType runtime instance created for data with content type application/octet-stream") and the flow completes. The bad body only fails when a page reads the answer. So guard the parse with `responseStatusCode.is2xxStatusCode()`, and put an ErrorHandler on the send step for the no-connection case (pmd-gotchas #85 has the full pattern).
- `.wrapSoapV11()` - auto-adds SOAP envelope + WS-Security header; `chars.newline()/space()`; `documents.documentId(id).get().asCSV()/getFilename()`
- **Additional sample-confirmed helpers (canonical DevRel flows, 2026-08-07) - fold these into generated flows and builder scripts:**
  - status/fault guards: **`data.<Send>.responseStatusCode.is2xxStatusCode()`** and **`response.isSoapFault()`** - the clean success/fault tests that pair with the 4xx-silent-failure caveat above (prefer over a bare `== 200`). **Runtime-verified 2026-10-05 (a client app build c2384e82):** `if (<status>.is2xxStatusCode() || <optOut>) data.<Send>.response.asJSON() else "<json text>".asJSON()` in a CreateValues Json param builds and runs; the `if ... else` form, `||`, `.not()`, `.equals("true")` on `data.start.headers.getHeader(...)` and `"...".asJSON()` on an interpolated string all work. A SendHttpRequest on `_DEFAULT_EXTERNAL_RETRY_CONFIG` does NOT fail on a 403/404 - the failure surfaces later, at `.asJSON()` of the HTML body - so guard the parse, not the send (pmd-gotchas #85).
  - XML: `stringAtXPathOrEmptyString(x)`, `stringAtXPathWithDefault(x,def)`, `countItemsAtXPath(x)`, `isValueAtXPath(x)`, `.exists("/a/b[1]")`.
  - JSON: `stringAtJsonPathOrEmptyString(x)`; `.iterator("$.data", 100)` takes an optional PAGE-SIZE 2nd arg. **`countItemsAtJsonPath("$.data")` counts the ARRAY as 1, not its elements - always use `$.data[*]` to count elements** (build-verified 2026-09-01, UAP Role Pairing).
  - dates: `zoneddatetime.now().plusDays(10)`, `<datetime>.format("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss")`, `datetime.now().toString()`.
  - strings: `.rightPad(n,ch)`, `.leftPad(n,ch)`, `.mkString(",")`, `.containsIgnoreCase(s)`, `.replaceIgnoreCase(a,b)`, `.length()`, `.lines()`, `.lowerCase()/.upperCase()`.
  - CSV read: `data.start.CSV.row(0).toStringList()`, `.rows(1)`, `.get(n)`, `.toBoolean()`.
  - refs/attrs: `instanceRef.integrationReference(id)`, `instanceRef.createReferenceList(idType,vals)`, `intsys.referenceAttributeValue(name,idType)`, `intsys.booleanAttributeValueWithDefault(name,false)`, `intsys.reportPath(name)`.
  - launch params: `lp.existsAndHasValue(x)`, `lp.integrationSystemId()`, `lp.sequencedValue(x)`, `lp.simpleData(x)`, `lp.referenceDataList(name,idType)`.
  - misc: `system.namedLogFile(name)`, `range(a,b)` (numeric-sequence generator), `math.plus(a,b)`, function-form `data.<node>.processingError.message()` / `.locationId()`, `List.stringList(...)`, document `.summary()`/`.name()`/`.asTEXT()`.

## Runtime limits - operationally critical

- **Sync orchestration triggered from a PMD page = 25 SECONDS hard cap.** Keep page-sync flows tiny; push real work to async / BP-triggered / Integration System flows.
- Sync total 5 min / async + Home Card 20 min / single continuous step 20 min / Integration System 48 hrs / BP callback window 90 days.
- "Wait for Long-Running API Responses" (26R1+, opt-in per SendWorkdayApiRequest): REST 1 hr / SOAP 6 hr via checkpoint+callback; each call resets the runtime clock; loop concurrency disabled when used in a loop. The 25-second page-sync cap still stands.
- Structural: 300 steps/orchestration (warn 200) / 150 flows/app (warn 125) / 200 MB in-memory / 2 GB file-backed / 20 MB launch message / 500 MB HTTP response.
- HTTP defaults: connect 10s / response 20s / overall 300s.

### Official corroboration & additions (official-docs - Workday Education course manuals, crawled 2026-08-25; spot-verify load-bearing numbers in-tenant)

- Manual's limits table: sync 5 min / async 20 min / response message 500 MB / launch message 20 MB / sync-from-presentation-page 25 s - all corroborate the verified numbers above. NEW number: run-log retention 30 days maximum.
- (!) reconcile - concurrent-data limits: the manual prints in-memory 20 MB / on-disk 500 MB vs our verified 200 MB in-memory / 2 GB file-backed above. Do NOT downgrade the verified numbers; treat the manual's smaller figures as possibly stale or a different measurement until spot-checked in-tenant.
- (!) reconcile - "Trigger Business Process (async only)": the manual restricts the Trigger Business Process component to ASYNC orchestrations. If a design assumes a sync flow can Trigger BP, build-verify first.
- Suborchestration prohibitions: Trigger Business Process and Send Workday RaaS Request are NOT allowed inside a suborchestration; suborchestrations are APP-scoped (reusable only across orchestrations in the same app).
- StoreDocument official defaults: retention P7D (7 days), and Store Document does NOT attach the file to the integration event unless explicitly configured (matches our `attachToIntegrationEvent: true` usage - set it deliberately).
- JoinLoop official strategy enums: multiple-match = Complete with Error / Skip Record / Use First / Use Last / Use All; missing-match = Alternate Processing / Complete with Error / Skip Record / Add Log; use `isDataDefined` inside the loop to detect a missing Join With output. Memory guidance: biggest dataset in Join On, smaller in Join With.
- lp.* launch-parameter catalog (official): lp.stringParam / booleanParam / numberParam / dateParam / dateTimeParam (returns ZonedDateTime) / simpleData (raw) / referenceData("p","ID_Type") / existsAndHasValue("p"). Manual best practice: guard with lp.existsAndHasValue BEFORE reading any optional parameter. Launch-param data types: Text, Boolean, Numeric, Date, DateTime + optional default.
- WQL corroboration: the total row cap per query is 1,000,000 (the LIMIT-clause max is 999,999 - see wql.md, the owner); manual's REST paging example is limit=1000&offset=0 (GET /data for short queries, POST /data with JSON body for long ones).
- Branch scope gotcha (official): values created INSIDE a Branch on Conditions branch are invisible outside it - put a Create Values with the SAME name on both sides when downstream steps need the value. Step Groups: only the LAST step's output in a group is available downstream.

## Auth model

Workday REST/SOAP/WQL/RaaS/Prism calls inside an orchestration are **auto-authenticated through the API Gateway via the ISU attached to the Integration System** - no API client, no OAuth header. REST needs only Report/Task domain permissions; only SOAP requires Integration Permissions. Sync/Home-Card flows can run as the launching user via the `AccessTokenFromInitiatingUser` credential variant - but use the ISU credential (`_DEFAULT_WORKDAY_CREDENTIAL`) for FDM/master-data writes. The API-client + refresh-token OAuth flow is for EXTERNAL callers and Extend-BO REST, not in-orchestration calls (see security-setup.md).

- **External OAuth from a flow - Integration CredStore (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified).** For an outbound `SendHttpRequest` to a third party that needs OAuth (not the auto-auth gateway), reference an **`OAuthCredential`** resource held in the Integration CredStore rather than pasting a token - the platform mints/refreshes the bearer and injects it. Flow-resource map (the named resource pools a flow declares and Send nodes reference): **credentials** (`WorkdayCredential` / `OAuthCredential` / external auth refs), **retryConfig** (`retryPolicies` - see the 4xx caveat), **tlsConfig** (`_DEFAULT_TLS_CONFIG`), **csvFormats** (`CsvFormat` for writes), and JSON/text template refs. Keeps secrets out of node bodies; the CredStore is the tenant-configured home for external OAuth (contrast the `attrstore.stringValue("subscriptionKey")` secret-proxy pattern below, which is for a simple static header key).

## The SOAP-write pattern (FDM master data is SOAP-only)

Node chain: `Log -> CreateValues -> CreateTextTemplate -> SendWorkdayApiRequest -> Log`.
- CreateTextTemplate holds the INNER operation XML only (e.g. `<bsvc:Put_Cost_Center_Request xmlns:bsvc="urn:com.workday/bsvc" bsvc:version="v46.1">...`), interpolating `{{data.CreateValues.x}}`.
- SendWorkdayApiRequest: POST, `path "/soap/v46.1/<Service>"`, body dataRef = `data.CreateTextTemplate.message.wrapSoapV11()`.
- Confirmed ops: `Put_Cost_Center`, `Put_Resource_Category`, `Submit_Gift`, `Submit_Project`, `Assign_Roles`, `Put_Benefit_Annual_Rate` (Benefits_Administration), `Increment_Sequence_Generator` (Integrations). Worktags pass by WID via `Related_Worktags_Data > Related_Worktags_by_Type_Data`. Op directory: Workday Community WWS index (v46.1+).
- `X-Validate-Only` header driven by a ValidationMode param = dry-run pattern.
- **Upsert via template conditional** (verified in a delivered production app, 2026-08-05): existence-check first (WQL), then wrap the reference element in `{{#if}}` - `{{#if data.CheckForExisting.exists}}<bsvc:Benefit_Annual_Rate_Reference>...</bsvc:Benefit_Annual_Rate_Reference>{{/if}}` - so one request updates when the instance exists and creates otherwise.
- **Tenant sequence numbers**: a sync flow POSTs `Increment_Sequence_Generator` to `/soap/v45.0/Integrations`, extracts `wd:Sequenced_Value` by XPath, and returns it to the page via `CreateJsonBody`. This is the tenant-native alternative to the counter-BO pattern (migration-aware, no race on a BO row) - present both when designing request-ID generation. **Simpler variant (confirmed 2026-08-07, `employeeDemographicOutbound/.../EmployeeDemographicFull.orchestration`):** when the sequence is wired as a launch parameter, read it directly with `lp.sequencedValue("Filename")` - no SOAP call at all. Prefer this for generated output filenames / request IDs when the integration's launch config supplies the sequence; fall back to the `Increment_Sequence_Generator` SOAP route when it doesn't.
- **Launching an external integration via SOAP from a flow (build+runtime-verified 2026-09-10, Inventory Expiry Export+Purge):** SOAP op `Launch_Integration_Event` at `/soap/v47.0/Integrations`. Critical gotchas on `Launch_Integration_Event_Request`: (a) `parent_id` + `parent_type` are REQUIRED on every `Launch_Parameter_Reference/ID` - without them Workday returns "Invalid ID value" and the launch fails. (b) Boolean params use `<wd:Boolean>1</wd:Boolean>` (or `0`) - NOT `<wd:Numeric>` - the WSDL maps Numeric to xsd:boolean but Workday rejects the strings "true"/"false" there with "value specified for Numeric is invalid". (c) Text = `<wd:Text>`, Date = `<wd:Date>` (xsd:date format), DateTime = `<wd:DateTime>`. (d) Maya `lp.*` data type WIDs (Boolean: `9d1e2089026a46308ed50f441ae3ea46`, Date: `6b7c8d95e82f4c3a9a730e31817ab966`) are NOT the same as Studio External Field WIDs - using Studio WIDs in `Put_Integration_System` causes "not a simple type" at runtime. Full schema: memory `[[soap-launch-parameter-schema]]`.

## Bulk BO writes from a flow - the verified BatchLoop -> `?bulk=true` contract

The canonical "page -> sync flow -> batched bulk write" shape (verified in delivered production apps, 2026-08-05). Page POSTs e.g. `{"postData":[...],"putData":[...]}` to `/launch`; the flow runs one `BatchLoop` per verb:

- `items = data.start.request.asJSON().iterator("$.postData[*]")` / `batchStrategy: SizeBasedBatchStrategy, size 100` / `foldValue: JsonFoldValue, nameProp "batch"`
- **BatchLoop strategies beyond size (confirmed 2026-08-07):** `SizeBasedBatchStrategy` (fixed count/batch - the default above), `GroupBatchStrategy` (batch by a key/group - use when each batch must contain all rows for one parent so a parent-level write isn't split across batches), and `CustomBatchStrategy` (custom split expression). Canonical `orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/BatchLoop_{Size,Group,Custom}Strategy.orchestration`.
- Each iteration sends ONE `SendWorkdayApiRequest` to `s"${"/apps/"}${context.appReferenceId()}${"/v1/<collection>?bulk=true"}"` with body `data.<Loop>.batch`.
- **`?bulk=true` works for PATCH and DELETE too, and BO REST PATCH is a partial update** (not just POST / PUT-full-replace / DELETE). One delivered flow multiplexes bulk POST/PATCH/DELETE off an `httpMethod` field in the request body.
- **Bulk-deleting children under a SINGLE_INSTANCE parent:** PATCH the parent first to drop the dependency, then bulk-DELETE the child rows. This is the delivered answer to "no clean bulk DELETE from a page submit" - the page's outbound endpoint calls a sync flow that does both.
- **Design note - human tollgate on volume syncs:** fire-and-forget bulk sync of external data is unacceptable at volume. The delivered pattern is a Review & Import selectable grid where already-imported rows appear LABELED (not hidden), and the user confirms the import set before the bulk write fires (verified in a delivered build session, 2026-08-05).

## The attachment-out pattern (extract a BO/document binary and send it externally)

The canonical way to pull a stored file (an attachment on an Extend BO, or a Workday-native document like a worker photo) OUT of Workday to an external destination - a data lake landing zone, or an ECM/content vendor like OnBase. **Build-verified against the Worker Photo Outbound O4I** (`WorkerPhotoOutbound.orchestration`; multi-record sibling `WorkerPhotosOutbound.orchestration`) - a known-good reference to copy. Node chain:

`GetParameters (CreateValues) -> [build fetch request: CreateTextTemplate] -> SendWorkdayApiRequest -> extract (CreateValues) -> BranchOnConditions -> CreateOutputFilename (CreateValues) -> StoreDocument -> Log`

- **Fetch the binary.** For a Workday-native doc: SOAP (Worker Photo uses `Get_Worker_Photos` -> POST `/soap/v45.0/Human_Resources`, auth `_DEFAULT_WORKDAY_CREDENTIAL`, retry `_DEFAULT_WORKDAY_RETRY_CONFIG`). For an **Extend BO attachment**: GET the attachment/`.attachment` BO instance via BO REST (returns the file **base64-encoded** + metadata), or a documents API. The binary always comes back base64.
- **Extract binary + metadata.** A CreateValues node pulls the base64 blob + original filename + extension out of the response - SOAP via `data.<Send>.response.asXML().stringAtXPath(".../wd:Worker_Photo/...")`; REST via `stringAtJsonPath(...)`. (Worker Photo captures `PhotoBase64`, `PhotoOrigFilename`, `PhotoFileExt`.)
- **Guard the empty case.** BranchOnConditions on "attachment exists" (and, in Worker Photo, on ID type to pick the right worker-ID XPath) - don't StoreDocument a null.
- **Build the output filename** with a CreateValues Scala-interp: `s"""${WorkerID}${FileName}.${PhotoFileExt}"""`.
- **Deliver via `StoreDocument`.** Key params (verified): `document` = the base64 source, `documentTitle` = the built filename, **`deliverFromDeliveryService: true`** (this is what pushes the file OUT - the transport is the integration's tenant-configured **Delivery Service**: SFTP to a data-lake landing zone, or HTTP to an ECM endpoint), `storageExpiresIn` e.g. `P7D`, `attachToIntegrationEvent: true` (keeps a copy on the event for audit), and `tags` for tracking. To push to an ECM's own REST API (e.g. OnBase) instead of the Delivery Service, swap the StoreDocument delivery for a `SendHttpRequest` posting the base64 + metadata.
- **Many attachments -> Loop.** The multi-record flow wraps the fetch+StoreDocument in a `Loop` (one iteration per record) and adds `LogToFile` for a run manifest. Use `BatchLoop` if batching.
- **Preserve the row<->file linkage** (keys/metadata in the filename or tags) so the external archive is reconstructable against the BO rows (wd-post-go-live retention story).

This is the pattern to mirror whenever an app stores attachments and the client wants them archived/sent externally - scope it as its own outbound integration (its own IDD line).

## Reading data at scale: RaaS vs WQL

- **RaaS** (`SendWorkdayRaasRequest` node - name source-verified, 2026-08-05): GET a custom report exposed as a web service; output XML/JSON/CSV/Excel (JSON shape `Report_Entry: [...]`); use for large structured extracts (500k+ rows). The report itself promotes separately from the app (wd-deployment). The report path/owner comes from `intsys.reportPath("<name>")` (or `intsys.stringAttributeValue("ReportCall")` = reportOwner/reportName) as an integration attribute. **URL-length guard (confirmed 2026-08-07, `employeeDemographicOutbound/.../EmployeeDemographicFull.orchestration`):** RaaS-over-REST query strings are limited to ~2083 chars, so a long multi-instance filter (e.g. a big `Workers!Employee_ID` list passed as a URL param) will fail - the sample pre-checks the param length (`<= 2000`) and errors early. Pass large filter sets by report prompt/POST rather than as a URL param.
- **WQL**: SQL-like, JSON only, targeted; LIMIT-clause max 999,999 (total row cap per query 1,000,000 - wql.md); REST paging `limit` default 20 / max 100 (up to 10,000 rows/page on the WQL endpoint). In a flow: either GET `/wql/v1/data` with the query in a `queryParams` entry (verified in a delivered production app), or build it in CreateTextTemplate and POST; iterate `.asJSON().iterator("$.data[*]")`.
- First-class paged components exist - the REST one is **`SendWorkdayRestApiPaginationRequest`** (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified: set `limit`/`offset`/`maxPages`, auto-`flatten`s pages into one dataset); the SOAP variant auto-wraps the envelope, don't also wrapSoap. Manual CreateValues+Send+Loop paging remains valid.
- **The per-item Loop idiom that ACTUALLY works (end-to-end verified 2026-08-05 - CORRECTS an earlier "iterator yields the whole array as one item" claim, which was a bad item reference, not a Maya limitation):**
  - `Loop.inputData`: type `["Iterator", ["Json", ...]]`, `isAuto: true`, source `data.<ReadNode>.response.asJSON().iterator("$.data[*]")`.
  - Inside the loop group, the CURRENT item is **`data.<LoopName>.item`** (LoopName = the Loop node's own name): `data.ResolveLoop.item.asJSON().stringAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.lineKey", emptyString())`. Referencing anything else is what produces the "whole array as one item / `$.x` never resolves" symptom.
  - Aggregate per-item output with a `JsonFoldValue` (`nameProp` e.g. `"output"`, data = `data.<TemplateNode>.message.asJSON()`) -> the folded array lands at `data.<LoopName>.output`.
  - Optional `Loop.filter` (`Expr[Boolean]`) works: `data.<Loop>.item.asJSON().stringAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.blueprint.id", emptyString()).equals("""<id>""")` narrows the iteration set.
  - Per-item transforms: build each element with a `CreateTextTemplate` (`{{expr}}` interpolation; nested triple-quoted `"""..."""` literals inside `{{}}` are fine), then fold - the clean element-by-element JSON transform.
  - Donor with the exact structure: `_reference/gq-bo-demo/getRestApiData.orchestration`. For pure bulk WRITES a single **bulk BO create** (`<collection>?bulk=true` with `{"data":[...]}`) is still simpler than looping per row.
  - **Other Loop-input builders (confirmed 2026-08-07):** `iterator.combineXMLIterators(iterA, iterB)` iterates TWO XML sources as one loop (`data.DATA1.message.iterator("/*/*")` + `data.DATA2.message.iterator("/*/*/*")`, canonical `orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/AnyLoop_CombineIterators.orchestration`); `range(a, b)` drives a counted loop over a numeric sequence (`range(1, 1000)` for a BatchLoop / synthetic-data generation, canonical `ImportProcessor.orchestration`).
- **In-loop string accumulation: use `CreateTextTemplate` + `TextFoldValue`, NOT `CreateValues` +
  `StringFoldValue`** (build-verified 2026-09-08, UAP v2 rpReconcileInt offset-paging; StringFoldValue
  shape fails the cloud compiler even when validate.py passes). The correct idiom (clone `DesiredSlice`
  in rpReconcileInt): (a) per-iteration fragment in a `CreateTextTemplate` body node, message e.g.
  `{{ s"${","}${data.<Loop>.item.asJSON().toString()}" }}`; (b) loop aggregate is a `TextFoldValue`
  (data = `data.<FragNode>.message`, failOnEmptyStream=false, condition null); (c) consume with
  `isDataDefined("<Loop>","<nameProp>")` guard + `.toString()`. **Nested loops:** the outer fold must
  read a `CreateTextTemplate` BODY NODE that captures the inner loop's TextFoldValue output -- the
  outer fold reading the inner aggregate directly is the failing shape. Example inner node:
  `{{ if (isDataDefined("<InnerLoop>","frag")) data.<InnerLoop>.frag else "" }}`.
- **`Loop.item` is typed `Any` -- ALWAYS `.asJSON()` before any jsonpath or `.toString()` access**
  (build-verified 2026-09-08; `data.<Loop>.item.asJSON().stringAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.offset","0")`).
  Skipping `.asJSON()` fails at runtime even when the item is clearly a JSON object.
- **Offset-paging a BO REST collection (shape-preserving recipe, build-verified 2026-09-08):** build a
  `CreateValues` String param `{"pages":[{"offset":0},{"offset":100},...,{"offset":9900}]}` (100 pages /
  up to 10k rows) -> outer `Loop` over `.pages.asJSON().iterator("$.pages[*]")` -> inner `GET` at
  `?limit=100&offset=${item...stringAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.offset","0")}` -> inner row-loop folds
  `",{row}"` via TextFoldValue -> outer TextFoldValue folds page fragments -> wrap:
  `if (isDataDefined(...).not() || rows.toString().isBlank()) "{\"data\":[]}" else
  s"${"{\"data\":["}${rows.toString().substringAfter(",")}${"]}"}"`. Past-end pages return
  `{"data":[]}` 200 and fold to nothing (no numeric-compare total-gating needed; `>=` in expressions
  is unproven in these flows). **DO NOT clone the toolkit donor `RESTPagedGet.orchestration` directly**
  -- it is flowVersion 2.12.0 with `data("X","Y")` expression syntax incompatible with our apps; borrow
  only the algorithm, use same-version local envelopes for node shapes.
- **Number extraction: `.toInt()` on a JsonPath string FAILS to compile** ("Function toInt cannot be applied to an instance of StringType"). Use `numberAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.relStartDays", 0)` to get a number directly (defaults on absent fields); it feeds `date.parse(...).plusDays(<number>)` cleanly - chain a second `.plusDays(...)` for begin + duration = end. (Verified end-to-end 2026-08-05.)
- **BUT: `numberAtJsonPath*` only works on fields BO REST serializes as numbers - INTEGER yes, DECIMAL no.** A DECIMAL field arrives as a JSON STRING, so `numberAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.estHours",0)` fails at render ("Expected number but found string") - and the failure mode is nasty: the flow **"completes with error"** rather than hard-failing, the template comes out empty, the bulk POST body is empty, and 0 records get created with no visible error except in the EndSync body / the missing rows. Read DECIMALs with `stringAtJsonPath*` and coerce where needed. (!) partially resolved: carrying a DECIMAL value INTO a bulk-create template body (string-read + emit-unquoted) still errored at render in the observing session (possibly field typing, possibly a stale deploy - not isolated). Until confirmed: model the field as INTEGER where the domain allows, or write the decimal via a follow-up PATCH instead of fighting the typing mid-template.
- **String literals in Maya expressions must be DOUBLE-quoted.** A single-quoted `'-M'` parses as a CHARACTER literal (exactly one char) and fails compile with "Native parser error: unclosed character literal". Use `"-M"` or triple-quoted `"""..."""` - bites hardest inside `{{ }}` template interpolations. (Verified 2026-08-06.)
- **BO collection reads inside a Loop: filter server-side or lose rows.** The 100-row GET cap truncates silently (no error) - use the reference-field query param `?<field>=<WID>` per iteration (e.g. `blueprintTasks?blueprint=<id>`); the dotted `?<field>.id=<WID>` form does NOT filter. Details in model.md REST section. (Verified 2026-08-06 - a 111-row import dropped its tail with no error.)
- **Caveat - WQL instance fields don't expose `.descriptor` INSIDE a flow (HIGH).** Even though the WQL REST response shows `name:{descriptor,id}`, inside an orchestration `stringAtJsonPath("$.name.descriptor")` won't resolve. Alias a FLAT scalar column in the WQL (e.g. `projName`) so the row is directly usable. (Orchestration-flow analog of pmd-gotchas #17, which covers the PMD-page case.)

## More verified flow patterns (delivered production apps, 2026-08-05)

- **Scheduled batch job (reference shape):** `IntegrationFrameworkTrigger -> WQL config read -> SendWorkdayRaasRequest -> BatchLoop -> JoinLoop (join per-record data against config) -> bulk POST rows -> per-row POST /v1/<bpNameLowerCamel>Events (launch a Model BP from the flow) -> bulk PATCH back-writes -> LogToFile + StoreDocument run manifest`.
- **External-API secret proxy:** page POSTs `{params, body}` to a sync flow; the flow reads them via `data.start.request.asJSON()`, calls `SendHttpRequest` with a secret header from `attrstore.stringValue("subscriptionKey")` (`auth: null`), and `EndSync` returns `data.<Send>.response` verbatim. The flow holds the secret - tighter than putting the API key in a PMD endpoint, where any page maintainer can read it.
- **Write-back-status loop (BP-triggered):** loop the request rows -> SOAP op per row (e.g. `Assign_Roles`) -> detect SOAP fault by XPath -> PATCH each row's status (success/failed) back onto the BO so the UI shows per-line outcomes.
- **In-tenant notification from a flow:** `POST /connect/v2/sendMessage` with a CreateTextTemplate body - the answer to "notify a user from an orchestration". (Version reconcile: the local schema snapshot is **connect v2** (`connect_v2_*.json`, path `/sendMessage`) and rest-api-catalog.md lists connect v2 - use **v2**; an earlier `/connect/v1/sendMessage` note here was stale drift.)
- **Graph (GraphQL) write from a flow:** a `.maya.FlowSync` flow can POST `/graphql/v1` - build the `{query, variables}` doc in a `CreateJson`, `SendWorkdayApiRequest` POST it (auth `_DEFAULT_WORKDAY_CREDENTIAL`), and return `responseStatusCode` + body. A single mutation document can combine multiple standard-object writes in one request (spot bonus = feedback + one-time payment in one call). Full authoring depth - provider shape, query-vs-mutation, the ref-id portability gotcha, HTTP-200+`errors[]` - is in **rest-api-catalog.md section  Graph API (GraphQL) authoring**. (Per Workday App Catalog sample createSpotBonus.)
- **Fetch a BO instance by reference ID instead of WID:** `GET .../v1/<collection>/${context.appReferenceId().capitalize()}_<BO>_ID=<value>` - the `<RefIdType>=<value>` pair is the path segment.
- **Flow-side BP-event -> target BO resolution (per Workday App Catalog samples, sample-verified - the orchestration analog of model-bp.md's page-side WQL lookup):** inside a BP-triggered (or BP-event-handling) flow, `GET .../v1/<bpNameLowerCamel>Events/<eventId>` and read `$.businessProcessTarget.id` to get the WID of the BO the event fired on - then GET that BO to act on it. The flow-side path to "which record is this approval about" without a WQL round-trip.
- **Two-pass dated import (parent/child hierarchy from template lines - end-to-end verified 2026-08-05, 32 tasks/5 parents/27 children, all dates + links correct):** StartBasic params (ids + startDate via `data.start.$_x`) -> GET the template-lines collection -> **Pass A (parents):** Loop with filter `...stringAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.parentLineKey", emptyString()).isBlank()` (+ the template-id match), per line a CreateTextTemplate builds the full record with resolved dates (`date.parse(data.start.$_startDate,"""yyyy-MM-dd""").plusDays(numberAtJsonPathWithDefault("$.relStartDays",0))`), JsonFoldValue -> bulk POST `?bulk=true` (`PostMains`) -> **Pass B (children):** same loop with `.isBlank().not()`, each child resolves its `parentTask` by a **JSONPath FILTER against Pass A's create response**: `data.PostMains.response.asJSON().stringAtJsonPathWithDefault(s"${"$.data[?(@.body.blueprintLineKey=='"}${<parentLineKey expr>}${"')].body.id"}", emptyString())` -> bulk POST children.
  - **KEY general finding: `stringAtJsonPath` SUPPORTS JSONPath filter expressions `[?(@.field=='value')]`** - the join-without-a-nested-Loop mechanism.
  - Bulk-create response shape: `{ total, data: [ { body: { ...created fields incl. id... }, status: 201 } ] }` - so `$.data[?(@.body.<sentKey>=='X')].body.id` returns the created record's id keyed by any field you sent.
- **WWS high-volume Import framework runs NATIVELY in O4I (confirmed 2026-08-07 - REFUTES the old "Studio-only" gap).** The full submit -> poll -> harvest-messages -> audit-file loop that Studio's import framework provides is now doable in an orchestration: build `Import_<Object>` (e.g. `Import_Supplier_Invoice`), POST to `/soap/v43.0/Resource_Management`, drive dry-run with an `X-Validate` header (`if XvalidateMode "1" else "0"`), and read the import ID from `Put_Import_Process_Response/Import_Process_Reference/ID[@wd:type="WID"]`. Then a second flow polls `Get_Import_Processes`, checks `Has_Messages == "1"`, pages `Get_Import_Process_Messages` via `SendWwsPaginationApiRequest`, and writes an `ImportResults.csv` audit file. Canonical donors: `supplierInvoicesInbound/orchestration/INT_Supplier_Invoices_Orch_Inbound.orchestration` + `INT_Check_Import_Result_Orch.orchestration`; also `orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/ImportProcessor.orchestration`. This changes O4I-vs-Studio decisioning for any bulk WWS-import integration (payroll input, invoices, journals) - see the updated gap note in wd-integration-dev studio.md.
- **Named run-audit log FILE - `LogToFile` + `system.namedLogFile(name)` (confirmed 2026-08-07).** Beyond `LogToFile for a run manifest` mentioned above, this is the first-class audit-file mechanism: declare a named log (`system.namedLogFile("InvoiceLog")` -> stored as `InvoiceLog.csv`), append rows across the run with `LogToFile`/`LogToFileValue` nodes, and `StoreDocument` the result at the end (canonical `supplierInvoicesInbound/...`, `updateServiceDateBoomerang/.../UpdateServiceDatesBoomerang.orchestration` writes `SuccessLog.txt`/`ErrorLog.txt`). This is the O4I analog of Studio's cloud-log rollup - use dual success/error logs on any bulk write so per-row outcomes survive the run.
- **Composite hierarchical sortable ID (end-to-end verified 2026-08-06, 3 projects / 32+19+19 tasks):** build human-readable ids that sort project->parent->child lexically: `P####` project code as prefix, parents `-M<nn>`, children `-M<parentNN>-T<nn>`, all fixed-width zero-padded (`P0001-M01-T03`). The import derives M/T numbers from 2-digit-padded template line keys (parents `"01"`, children `"01-02"`) and reads the project code via a ReadProject GET node before the loops. Remember the string pieces are double-quoted: `{{ code + "-M" + n }}`.

## Newer capabilities (DevCon 2026 - verify GA before client use)

- **Prism Materialize**: `POST /api/prismAnalytics/v3/tables/materialize` `{source, target, operation: Insert|TruncateAndInsert}` - apiName-keyed (tenant-portable), auto callback (zero timeout risk). Alternative: fileContainers + dataChanges (DCT) choreography.
- **SFTP Transport File** node (Retrieve/Deliver/List/Delete; creds via Integration CredStore).
- **AWS SigV4 credential** on SendHttpRequest (Lambda/S3 direct).
- **Kill Orchestration** (Activity Dashboard or API): bypasses checkpoints, does NOT roll back external writes - incidents only.
- **Agent Actions**: a `.maya.FlowSync` flow exposed as an MCP tool via `mcpToolConfig` (MCPToolInputConfig on start, MCPToolOutputConfig on end; flat JSON in/out; descriptions ARE the LLM tool schema - write them well). Endpoint: `POST https://api.<region>.wcp.workday.com/orchestrate/v1/apps/<appId>/mcp`.

## Debugging

Run Logs are `wd_*` fields - filter `wd_log_type = remote`, read `wd_response_code`/`wd_message` for API-call failures; `wd_level` and `wd_env` (PROD/SANDBOX/IMPL) also searchable. Local Disk Sync is unreliable for orchestrations - use `wdcli upload`/`download` for O4I.

- **[BV] `wdcli app validate` does NOT exist as a command** - the real validator is `wdcli app upload` (the upload IS the build/validate step). **`wdcli app delete` does NOT exist either** - delete an app via the Developer Site console UI. Do not script either command; they fail as unknown commands, not as app errors.

- **Visualize a flow (community tool - fastest way to READ a `.orchestration`).** `.orchestration`/`.suborchestration` files are deeply-nested, single-line typed-wrapper JSON that is near-unreadable in a text editor. The **Orchestrate Flow Viewer** (VS Code / Cursor extension, publisher `ekwuno`; MIT; **community/unofficial - not a Workday product**) renders an exported O4I project - a folder with `appManifest.json` + an `orchestration/` dir - as an interactive diagram: trigger -> steps -> branches -> loops -> error handlers, click a step to inspect its assignments/conditions/loop iterators, **Call-Subflow** cards that navigate to the referenced flow across the workspace, and a diagram<->pretty-JSON toggle. It is **read-only** (the Workday Orchestration Builder stays the source of truth); reach for it to understand/review/audit a flow quickly, especially right after a `wdcli app download` when reviewing an existing app (see app-review-audit.md). Install the `.vsix` via "Extensions: Install from VSIX...". Source: github.com/Ekwuno/workday-orchestrate-viewer. (As a community tool, confirm current behavior/security before relying on it for client work.)

- **Declarative mock-response test harness (confirmed 2026-08-07 - a low-cost unit-test path the suite previously didn't mention).** You can preview/test a PMD page OR an orchestration-backed outbound endpoint against a FIXED response without hitting the live API. Two file types under `presentation/testing/`: a `<name>.mock_config` maps a call site to a mock - `{"mappings":[{"location":{"pmdId":"<page>","endPointName":"<endpoint>"},"mockId":"<id>"}]}` - and a `<name>.mock_response` holds the canned payload - `{"id":"...","responseCode":200,"responseBody":{...}}`. Canonical `vehicleRegistration/presentation/testing/` and `AWSBadgeGenerator/presentation/testing/`. Note it keys on `pmdId`+`endPointName` (a PMD/App-Builder test facility), so it's as much a page-testing tool as an orchestration one - reach for it to test error/edge responses deterministically.

Two more verified diagnostics (delivered build session, 2026-08-05):

- **Direct-launch diagnostic:** invoke a flow directly with `POST {apiGatewayEndpoint}/orchestrate/v1/apps/<refId>/orchestrations/<name>/launch` (body `{}`) - the response carries the EndSync body INCLUDING error messages that a page-side call often swallows.
- **DIAG re-point:** temporarily point the EndSync body at an intermediate node to inspect that node's output directly, then restore the real body before redeploying.
- **No-API spike flow (autonomous expression verification):** to prove an expression-language behavior without touching real APIs or a PMD trigger, deploy a tiny `StartBasic -> EndSync` flow whose EndSync body dataRef IS the expression under test, launch it via the direct-launch POST above with a tenant bearer token (`wdcli tenant token`), and read the response body as the probe result. Build-clean = linter accepts it; 200 body = runtime truth. This is how the date-arithmetic behavior above was verified - use it whenever a reference says "shape unverified."

## Reading DELIMITED FILES in a flow - what is dynamic, what is not (verified 2026-08-06)

Censused **1,347 expressions across 57 flow files** in the local reference corpus. This settles the
recurring question "can the integration just read the client's file?"

**Reading CAN be dynamic. Field mapping cannot.**

- The only CSV column accessor is **`columnValueAtIndex(n)`** - purely POSITIONAL. Used with a
  `CreateJson` node holding a `Mapping` list (`gq-bo-demo/csvToJson.orchestration`).
- There is **no name-based column accessor**, **no list `.indexOf()`**, and **no Loop index/counter
  CONFIG KEY** (verified Loop/BatchLoop keys: name, isDisabled, errorHandler, inputData, filter,
  aggregateNode, earlyStopCondition, sorts, locale, group, notes, batchStrategy, foldValue). So you
  cannot resolve a column position from its header name at runtime. Scope note: this census
  covered CONFIG keys only - the RUNTIME `data.<Loop>.itemNumber` counter (sample-verified, see
  Node vocabulary) is an output, not a config key, so both findings hold. Same status both places:
  sample-verified; build-verify in-tenant before production reliance.
- **`.asCSV()` works with an EMPTY `csvFormats` resource map** - a declared `CsvFormat` is not
  required to READ a file. Declared formats are for WRITING (e.g. the error log).

### The header-driven reader (the supplier-invoice template - copy this)

`_reference/supplier-invoice-template/orchestration/` (referenceId `supplierinvoiceinboundtemplate_<org>`)
reads a variable-layout delimited file without a compiled schema:

```
documents.labels(DocumentTags).getDocumentIds()      # pick up by TAG, not filename
documents.documentId(id).get().asCSV()
ValidateFile:      data.start.Data.firstLine().equals(data.start.ExpectedHeader)
                   data.start.Data.countRows().greaterThan(1)   -> ContinueOnConditions halts
ConvertCSVtoJSON:  GetHeader   = data.start.Data.firstLine().split("|")   # names read AT RUNTIME
                   csvLoop     = data.start.Data.rows(1)                  # skip the header
                   CreateArray = data.csvLoop.item.toString().split("|", true)
                   ArraySize vs csvHeader.size()                          # per-row column check
                   CreateJSON (TextTemplate) -> Aggregate into a JSON array
```

Tenant-side config: `intsys.stringAttributeValue("Expected Header" | "Document Tags" |
"Web Service" | "Web Service Version")` + `lp.booleanParam("Validation Mode")`. A client changing
their column layout is then an **Integration Attribute edit, not a code change**.

### Consequences for design

- A client **cannot omit columns** from a positional layout. Push expansion into a pre-formatter
  (Workday Document Transformation is the standard pre-formatter) that blank-fills to the full column set.
- **O4I cannot read Excel or fixed-width at all**, and cannot branch parsing per record type
  (header/detail/trailer). Those REQUIRE a pre-formatter - no configuration substitutes.
  - **WRITE is different - O4I CAN produce an `.xlsx` (CONFIRMED 2026-08-07).** An `.xlsx` is a zip of OOXML parts, so a flow emits one by building the `sheetN.xml`/`rId` part contents from CSV rows (XML-escaping cells via `.replaceIgnoreCase("&","&amp;")...`), folding with `XmlFoldValue`, and assembling with `ZipArchiveFoldValue`. Canonical donors: `orchestrateForIntegrationsSampler/orchestration/CreateExcel.suborchestration` + `CreateSingleSheet.suborchestration`. The READ side stays "cannot" - no native Excel PARSER exists; this is output-only, a build-the-parts-by-hand technique, not a `.asExcel()` helper.
  - **WRITE also covers fixed-width AND declarative CSV (CONFIRMED 2026-08-07).** Fixed-width output: per column `data.<node>.<field>.rightPad(50, chars.space()).substring(0, 50)` then `TextFoldValue`. Declarative delimited output: `CsvFormat` / `CsvColumn` / `CsvFormatRef` + `FormattedCsvFoldValue` (branch on a launch param like `lp.simpleData("Output File Type")` to switch layouts). Canonical `locationChangesOutbound/orchestration/OutputTransform.orchestration`, `employeeDemographicOutbound/.../EmployeeDemographicFull.orchestration`. So O4I now covers the WRITE side of fixed-width/delimited outputs that previously implied Studio/DT.
  - **O4I as a POST-PROCESSOR on a delivered Core Connector / EIB (CONFIRMED 2026-08-07).** A flow can pick up the file a delivered Core Connector produced (`documents.labelsMatchAny(List.stringList("Deliverable")).get()`) and reformat it (fixed-width or a specific delimited layout) - bolted onto the CC's BP. A cheap conversion win: keep the CC for the extract, add a small O4I to reshape the output, instead of rebuilding the whole extract in Studio. (`locationChangesOutbound` is the donor.)
- For repeating structures, use a **packed column** - `TYPE=VALUE;TYPE=VALUE` parsed in the flow.
  Adding a new type then needs no header change (a header change is breaking: every client's
  pre-formatter must move in the same release). Guard the delimiter: it must not collide with the
  packed separators.

## Finding a Workday SOAP operation's real schema - the docs ARE public

`references/rest-api-catalog.md` notes the REST directory is login-gated. The **SOAP operation
pages are NOT** - they are on Community file-hosting and fetch cleanly without auth:

```
https://community.workday.com/sites/default/files/file-hosting/productionapi/<Service>/<version>/<Operation>.html
e.g. .../productionapi/Payroll/v46.1/Import_Payroll_Input.html
```

Swap service, version and operation. This gives the full child-element list, document ORDER, and
cardinality (`[0..1]`, `[0..*]`, `choice`). The sibling `<Service>.xsd` exists but is usually too
large to fetch in one request. **Go here first** rather than reverse-engineering from Studio XSLTs -
one fetch replaced hours of source archaeology.

**Cross-check what you read** against real local usage. Doing that caught that Workday's worktag ID
types follow no single convention: `Fund_ID`, `Grant_ID`, `Project_ID`, `Business_Unit_ID`,
`Location_ID` are plain `_ID` while `Cost_Center_Reference_ID`, `Region_Reference_ID`,
`Gift_Reference_ID` carry `_Reference_ID`. Never infer an ID type from the element name.

**Import_ vs Submit_/Put_ (client rule, verified):** use the **`Import_*`** operation when loading
from a **file** - it is bulk, taking a request-level default plus MANY data children in one call.
`Submit_*` / `Put_*` are singular-transaction services for BP-triggered integrations. Both names
appear for the same object, so this is easy to get wrong. (Reconciliation, official-docs - Workday
Education Studio course manual, crawled 2026-08-25: submit-type ops are best "for up to 200 records
(sometimes more, depending on the operation)"; imports are "reserved for high volumes (thousands of
objects)" - consistent with this rule, and adds the ~200-record number.)
